replacements.before: the constancy $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ requires the vanishing side-flux hypothesis of [F8] and is not implied by zero divergence alone.
replacements.after: write their sum as $\mathcal F^b(s_1,s_2)$, with the same signed faces as in the Statement. Thus $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=-\mathcal F^b(s_1,s_2)$ by clause (b) of [F8]. Equality of the two slice totals is therefore equivalent to $\mathcal F^b(s_1,s_2)=0$, and constancy throughout $[c_0,d_0]$ is equivalent to this equality for every $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$. The facewise-zero hypothesis in clause (c) of [F8] forces every side integral to vanish and hence is sufficient. It is not necessary: take the zero Maxwell fields and sources, and the constant adopted matter tensor $T_{\mathrm m}=\operatorname{diag}(0,P,0,0)$ with $P\ne0$. It is $C^1$, symmetric and divergence-free; all $Q^b$ are zero, while for $b=1$ the integrals on the two $x^1$ side faces are both the nonzero number $P(s_2-s_1)(d_2-c_2)(d_3-c_3)$ and cancel in their signed difference. Zero divergence alone supplies the balance identity, not a guarantee that the net side flux vanishes.
